## Findings
- claim-1: \(I_{r,q}=\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbb Z}\{s_\lambda:\lambda\nsubseteq q^r\}\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) has Schur classes indexed by \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-218]
- claim-2: For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), and \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\); the lower family is indexed by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- claim-3: Partition conjugation is a ring involution and sends \(I_{r,n-r}\) to \(I_{n-r,r}\). [source-2@L1756-L1772|claim=formal-document]
- claim-4: Under \(r=j+c,\ q=i+p,\ i,j\ge1,\ p,c\ge0\), conjugation induces \(\Lambda/I_{q,r}\cong\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), transports the interval ideal and \(A_+J\), and sends the lower family for \((q,r,j,i,c,p)\) bijectively onto the right family for \((r,q,i,j,p,c)\).
## Strategy
Put \(A_{r,q}=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), with \(I_{r,q}\) the Schur-span outside \(q^r\). Since
\[
\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q,
\]
\(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\). Hence
\[
\omega_{r,q}:A_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{q,r},\qquad
\bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}
\]
is a graded ring isomorphism (and its own inverse).

For the interval ideal
\[
J_{r,q}^{i,j}:=\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda ,
\]
Littlewood–Richardson containment shows it is an ideal: every Schur term in
\(s_\alpha s_\lambda\) contains \(\lambda\), hence contains \(i^j\), unless it vanishes outside \(q^r\). Moreover,
\[
\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q}^{i,j})=J_{q,r}^{j,i},
\]
because \(\lambda\supseteq i^j\iff\lambda'\supseteq j^i\). Since \(\omega\) preserves degree,
\[
\omega_{r,q}((A_{r,q})_+)=(A_{q,r})_+,\qquad
\omega_{r,q}((A_{r,q})_+J_{r,q}^{i,j})
=(A_{q,r})_+J_{q,r}^{j,i}.
\]

Now assume
\[
r=j+c,\qquad q=i+p,\qquad i,j\ge1,\quad p,c\ge0,
\]
and set \(a=\min(p,c)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). The lower family for
\((q,r,j,i,c,p)\) is
\[
\mathcal L=\{\bar s_{(j^i,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}.
\]
For \(\rho\subseteq b^a\),
\[
(j^i,\rho)'=(\,i+\rho'_1,\ldots,i+\rho'_b,i^{\,j-b}\,),
\]
where \(\rho'\subseteq a^b\). Thus conjugation gives the bijection
\[
\mathcal L\longrightarrow
\mathcal R:=
\{\bar s_{((i+\tau_1,\ldots,i+\tau_b),i^{\,j-b})}:
\tau\subseteq a^b\},
\]
which is precisely
\[
\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\},
\]
the right-adjoined family for \((r,q,i,j,p,c)\).

For bigrassmannian admissibility, the original parameters may be written
\[
n=r+q,\quad t=c+1,\quad s=c+i,
\]
and the swapped ones as
\[
n=q+r,\quad \widetilde t=p+1,\quad \widetilde s=p+j.
\]
The inequalities
\[
1\le t\le r,s\le n,\qquad t>r+s-n
\]
follow respectively from \(i,j\ge1\), \(p,c\ge0\); explicitly,
\(t>r+s-n\) is \(c+1>c-p\).  After swapping, they become
\[
1\le\widetilde t\le q,\widetilde s\le n,\qquad
\widetilde t>q+\widetilde s-n,
\]
with the strict inequality \(p+1>p-c\).  The valid-tuple inequalities are likewise preserved:
\[
a+j\le r,\qquad a+i\le q,\qquad b\le i,j,
\]
and, after interchange, these are the same two inequalities in reverse order. If the nondegenerate valid-tuple convention requires \(a\ge1\), this additionally requires \(p,c\ge1\); the conjugation certificate itself remains valid when \(a=0\).

Thus the requested standalone parameter-conjugation target is established.

## Gaps
None for the stated conjugation, interval, family, and admissibility certificate.
